newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crude rises modestly in late trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crude rises modestly in late trade.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crudes rose modestly late Thursday, as differentials were unchanged and prices for West Texas Intermediate (WTI) firmed amid a supply squeeze.
Dealers failed to strike deals for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude Thursday, whose discount off WTI remained minus $1.70 a barrel.
Outright ANS prices, reacting to flat diffs and higher WTI, rose 50 cents to $24.75/24.95 a barrel.
Producers said three buyers bid for ANS, which was offered $1.60 under.
"With the Merc (New York Mercantile Exchange) up as fast as it is a lot of people are stepping back," a producer said.
Line 63 crude was thin, with no fixed basis deals and posted plus values stagnant at $0.95 to $1.05.
Kern River prices rose with higher posted prices, hitting $18.40/18.50 a barrel, a 25 cent gain.
Discounts remained 10 cents below to even with postings, traders said.
Wilmington crude, produced offshore in Long Beach, Calif., also rose 20 cents with postings to $19.85/19.95.
